_comment: doc-ref-integrity allowlist. A canon doc may legitimately cite a path absent on disk: runtime-generated artifacts, frozen/per-version capsules, removed-by-design dead-tree paths (the live-CODE layer is guarded by cutover-completeness.js), planned/aspirational scripts named in ROADMAP/MC, historical change-log/ADR descriptions, or per-domain-generated scaffolds. List target PREFIXES (startsWith, forward slashes) and exact LITERALS. Per-line `<!-- doc-ref-ignore -->` in the doc is the inline escape hatch for self-documenting/anti-example lines. Keep this honest — every entry must read as 'this path is SUPPOSED to be absent', not 'I don't want to fix it'. Prefer fixing a genuine navigational stale ref over allowlisting it.
_note_gitignored_by_design: The entries tagged here — pathPrefix `.claude/agents/president/_system/beta/mined/` (raw /beta:mine output, .gitignore), plus the literal `.claude/settings.local.json` (the per-machine settings layer; untracked, compiled INTO .claude/settings.json by scripts/mc/settings/compile.js) — are per-machine files that a FRESH CLONE (a CI runner, a new worktree) never has. The citing docs are correct (several even say 'gitignored' inline); the targets are SUPPOSED to be absent on a clean tree, the same category as the `.claude/project/memory/` prefix. Enforcer for the class: the PER-MACHINE test in doc-ref-integrity.test.js asserts these targets are allowed-absent under this shipped allowlist regardless of machine state.
_note_install_time: Exact literals the setup and scaffold steps write into a project: .claude/framework-installed.json, PROJECT.md, _mc/MANIFEST.json, and the optional _mc/settings/defaults.json that bootstrap copies when its layout carries one. They are absent from a source checkout and from the product tree before setup, so a doc that cites them is correct. Exact paths only, never a prefix.
